Bogus Bishops

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Doctor, Professor, Chancellor, Archbishop Edward van der Berg is a self-proclaimed General of God, but the long arm of the law has caught up with him for running a bogus university

Unique Selling Point:
Prophets for profit.
Edward van den Berg is a self-appointed Visionary who received a “commission from God" to establish the Immanuel Theology Institute International, formerly known as the Immanuel University of Theology International. That was until 2018 when the Department of Higher Education and Training demanded that van den Berg cease to call it a “university”, as all South African universities are organs of state. Nevertheless there are now 50 (FIFTY) Immanuel campuses across South Africa - from the Immanuel University of Orange Farm to the Immanuel University of Pongola – and another 26 campuses spread across Africa, from Madagascar to Nigeria, not to mention India and Russia.

But what do they mean by “campus”? And who runs them?

Professor Chancellor Archbishop van den Berg offers Certificates, Diplomas and Degrees, from Bachelors to Masters to Doctorates. And former alumni like Bishop Doctor Bernard Coopasamy of KZN (pictured with President Cyril Ramaphosa at the Law and Religious Communities in Africa conference in 2020)) who go on to open satellite campuses that offer the same courses.
But who recognises them? Immanuel Theology Institute is NOT accredited with SAQA. Why not? This is van den Berg’s reason:

i. The Christian Theology programs available at SAQA accredited training venues are all of the Trinity Based faith based doctrine of the Roman Catholic Church.
ii. We are a unique training Entity for Pentecostal, Charismatic and Free Churches that does not form part of the so called main stream churches that supported the Apartheid System or being part of the Roman Catholic Trinity (Three God Doctrine) doctrine of the Roman Cleric.


Summary:
Ironically, all the self-ordained Bishops and Archbishops are not averse to wearing the liturgical vestments and other paraphernalia that originated in the Roman Catholic church. So where does the Immanuel University/Institute buy their chasubles and mitres? The same place they buy their academic gowns and caps – Distinguished Cuts Mantles in downtown Joburg, who proudly list Archbishop Edward van den Berg as a client.

Immanuel University is not registered on the SAQA database and is not accredited to offer NQF-registered qualifications. Not to be discouraged van den Berg simply created his own organisation:
CTQA (Christian Theology Quality Assurance Association (Pty) Ltd,

This entity was allegedly registered with CIPRO by Chancellor Professor Archbishop van den Berg in 2018. Bishop Coopasamy is the Vice-President.

Immanuel’s website gives a long list of other accrediting institutions, but a cursory check proves these claims to be false:
Theology Accreditation International does not exist, and Theological Accreditation International has never heard of them.
COMENSA has never heard of them.
American Accrediting Association of Theological Institutions (A.A.A.T.I.) does not credit any institution outside the USA
Ballsbridge University is is listed as a bogus university by the DHET.

On the list of Affiliations:
the SA Christian Religious Council does not exist, nor does their NPO number.
The SA Pentecostal Bishops Council (non-existent NPO number) is led by Professor Mbulelo Dyasi, another graduate of Immanuel University.
The SA Council of Churches has never heard of them

Ironically, all the self-ordained Bishops and Archbishops are not averse to wearing the liturgical vestments and other paraphernalia that originated in the Roman Catholic church. So where does the Immanuel University/Institute buy their chasubles and mitres? The same place they buy their academic gowns and caps – Distinguished Cuts Mantles in downtown Joburg, who proudly list Archbishop Edward van den Berg as a client.


Further information:
The NQF Amendment Act of 2019:
(4) Any person, education institution, skills development provider,
foreign institution is guilty of an offence if it falsely claims to be registered
and accredited as an education institution, skills development provider or
foreign institution in terms of the laws of the Republic or foreign law.
If found guilty van der Berg and his co-accused could be fined and face up to 5 years in prison.

However, the Immanuel website is still up and running and offering courses at it's various campuses.

Script:


PROPHETS FOR PROFIT

V/O: Pentecostal charismatic churches have become popular in South Africa for spontaneous outpourings of the Holy Spirit: singing, speaking in tongues and divine healing.

Bushiri: “Come out, out! Jesus said you are delivered.”

V/O: But they also attract so-called prophets who are more interested in profits.

A divine vision in 2010 launched the Immanuel University of Theology offering Diplomas, Bachelors, Masters and Doctorates in Divinity and Theology. These happy graduates were capped by the receiver of that vision: Doctor, Professor, Chancellor Edward van den Berg.
From a lowly Railways manager he transformed into a Pentecostal Archbishop.

VdBerg: “We heal the sick and the blind. We raise up the dead.”

V/O: Unsurprisingly, these miraculous achievements don’t all add up. So we paid him a visit at his retirement village in Boksburg.

Vd Berg: He made me an apostle in 2010.

Claire: Straight from God?

Vd Berg: Straight from God.

Claire: You became an apostle?

VD Berg: Then he said to me I’m an apostle. So a lot of people don’t believe. When the Lord talks he talks to you.

Claire: It was real?

VdBerg: Real for real. And that empowered me. And then he said to me I want you to train up the end time generals and uplift the previous marginalised and disadvantaged in society.

V/O: This inspired him to write the entire curriculum for the Immanuel University of Theology, aimed at educating uncertified pastors. With a genuine desire for formal qualifications they flocked to enrol.

VdBerg: I’ve got 64 campuses in South Africa and 20 internationally.

Claire: So if I had to go to a campus, I'm not going to see something like Wits?

VdBerg: No, no, no.

Claire: I'm going to see somebody's house?

Vd Berg: You, you're going to be at the church or you can be at the house or where the guy's got 3 x 3 tin shack.

Claire: Okay, I hear you.

VdBerg: 85% of the population are non-whites and they’re Pentecostal charismatics. So there was a demand and I was assigned to train these guys up.

Claire: So you are saving the black people?

VDBerg: Yes.

Claire: You are saving…

VDBerg: I’m a Moses for black people.

Claire: You are Moses for black people?

VDBerg: And I’m the one that I know I will go to the heavens. I’m not going to miss, because Moses made mistakes. I don’t make mistakes in that sense. I’m not prepared to sacrifice my anointing and my position. I’ve got a calling from God.

Claire: Does it not sound arrogant when you say you are the Moses for black people? Don’t you think it could sound arrogant?

VDBerg: No they see it as a benefit because somebody must take them out of the shambles.

Claire: So black people see you as a benefit?

VDBerg: I’m not saying Blacks, I say non-Whites.

Claire: Okay so people of colour love it when you say that you are their Moses?

VDBerg: I’m their Moses to lead them out of this situation where they never been recognized, they never got something. And we got thousands of churches in South Africa with leaders that are not qualified.

V/O: But is he leading them to the Promised Land or up the garden path? Van den Berg himself is not qualified because he studied at Therapon University – a bogus online college in the US Virgin Islands.

VDBerg: I started with my Bachelor, my Masters.

Claire: During that time?

VDBerg: And DTh, and a DD, and during that time in 2010 I was a PhD man.

V/O: But this long list of qualifications is worthless. And as for Immanuel University – it was never registered with the Department of Higher Education and Training, and is also listed as a bogus college.

Shaheeda: What the Immanuel University was doing was offering or awarding diplomas and degrees in theology to students. That’s illegal. But even worse was the use of the word university. The legislation doesn’t provide for private higher institutions to call themselves universities.

V/O: Dr Shaheeda Essack is the Director of Registrations who laid charges with the police last year.

Shaheeda: For the illegal awarding of a doctoral degree and the person charged was Mr EA van den Berg.

Claire: Can he call himself a Professor?

Shaheeda: No he cannot call himself a professor. Even registered higher institutions cannot confer professorships. It’s not allowed.

VdBerg: Mrs Essack sent me a letter and I must close the campuses down. I said I will maintain the Head Office. I’ve put 10 million into this business, my pension. I said I’m not going to let it go for nothing.

V/O: So, unable to pass through the eye of a needle, he simply changed the name from University to Institute and carried on trading.

VdBerg: I franchise. So the Immanuel University of Theology is a, it’s a franchise.

Shaheeda: Franchising itself is illegal. Even with registered private institutions, it’s not allowed. And so he’s obviously seen a market in the religious sphere, and he’s seen the desperation and he’s seen the ignorance and he is basically capitalizing on that.

V/O: We went undercover to Immanuel Institute’s Heidelberg campus to inquire about the fees. The franchisees introduced themselves as Dr Johan and Dr Lee.

Dr Lee: So it’s about R6000 a year for the first year. The second year also 6, third year 6. You can do it in ten consecutive payments, that’s 600. There is accreditation overseas, so we are recognised. And we are recognised through SAQA in South Africa.

V/O: But the truth will set you free. The South African Qualifications Authority verifies and registers all learning achievements in South Africa. They do not recognise any qualifications offered by Immanuel.

Nadia: Like everyone else they need to be part of the quality assurance regime, and this is really so the public can trust the integrity of the qualification itself. Our legislation in South Africa requires that all programmes that lead to qualifications must be registered on the NQF.

V/O: CEO Nadia Starr explains the NQF, or National Qualifications Framework, is a system that records all education levels approved by the quality councils. Immanuel’s programs don’t pass muster.

Nadia: In terms of what I’ve seen on the website, those qualifications are not registered on the NQF.

V/O: But Immanuel's website falsely claims that they are.

Claire: When you've got a program that is offered and at the bottom it said NQF4 what are you explaining? What are you saying to those people who are trying to apply to a program?

VdB: NQF4. So those are those 120 credits.

Claire: But those are not recognized by SAQA, are they?

Vd Berg: No, they get endorsed by them.

Claire: They endorsed by SAQA?

VdB: Yeah. They're SAQA moderators, assessors, and some of them become pastors with us. So these guys are SAQA, they got stamps. So our programs are stamped.

V/O: Who knows what stamps they’re collecting, but they’re not SAQA’s.

Nadia: I don't know the people that he refers to, but anyone working outside of the system, it would seem to me wouldn't have the mandates to make certain decisions. So for those people that have gone through a process that is not really legitimate, their qualifications wouldn’t be recognised.

Link: So what do you do when the South African qualifications authority doesn’t register the qualifications you’re dishing out? Well, if you’re a self-appointed Professor like Eddie van den Berg you don’t let that ruin your business plan. You simply create your own Qualifications authority: the CTQA.

V/O: Christian Theology Quality Assurance was registered by van den Berg in 2018 at this address in Boksburg. It’s also houses a sex shop, a gambling lounge and a bottle store – en route to the land of milk and honey liqueur.

Claire: So what’s the CTQA’s job?

VdB: They look after the accreditation of the programs and then when people do RPL, they look if they’ve got it.

Claire: So you create the program and they you also make sure that your own program is verified and accredited?

VdB: No, that is our teachings. The CTQA is to look at the Christian theology.

Claire: But the Christian theology they they’re looking at, it’s yours. It’s the programs that you’ve written?

VdB: The programs I wrote.

Claire: So the organization that you’ve created is the organization that then verifies the programs that you wrote.

VdB: That was the initial thing is that we need accreditation. Because I was asked what are you going to do with SAQA?

V/O: We showed the CEO one of the qualification forms issued by CTQA.

Nadia: Essentially what he’s done is taken the structure and even some of the wording of our qualifications from our national qualifications register and essentially appropriated it for content that is not quality assured.
And in fact even the preamble and some of the sections are in fact very much a copy and paste of our structure.

Shaheeda: This is the evidence that he has usurped the functions of SAQA, which is a statutory regulatory body, established in terms of the NQF Act. It wouldn’t be fair for me to say someone is mentally unstable or not okay up there. But this is fraud.

V/O: Yet “Prof" Edward refuses to acknowledge that Immanuel’s Diplomas and Degrees are not worth the paper they’re copied and pasted on.

Claire: That is not a registered or a recognized qualification that you are handing out.

VdB: No, I’m not saying so.

Claire: You don’t agree with that?

Eddie: No.

V/O: Talk about turning a blind eye to a burning bush.

Link: It’s like me starting the Derek Watts Dance Academy, or the Carte Blanche University of Sweetness and Light. Sign up now and I’ll get you a Doctorate by Easter.

VO: And once you’re a doctor, you can become a Bishop.

Claire: So how many Bishops have you ordained?

Eddie: I’ve done 12 bishops, of which say, six is Arches and six others. I was ordained or consecrated as a Bishop. That’s under the South African Bishops Council.
Pentecostal Bishops Council. I was the visionary of that.

Claire: Are you registered with the SA Council of Churches?

Eddie: No.

Claire: Why?

Eddie: Because they’re Trinitarians.

V/O: Instead he created the South African Christian Religious Council.

Claire: So the SA Religious Council of Churches is also your organization?

Eddie: That’s my NPO.

Claire: That’s your NPO?

Eddie: To make sure that we can ordain and appoint the pastors.

Claire: Is that NPO registered in South Africa? Is it recognised?

Eddie: Yeah.

V/O: But the NPO Certificate he supplied is fake.
We checked with the Department of Social Development and this NPO number actually belongs to Sitofini Pre-School in the Eastern Cape.
It seems this Archbishop may be an arch fraudster.

V/O: CEO Nadia Starr explains the NQF, or National Qualifications Framework, is a system that records all education levels approved by the quality councils. Immanuel’s programs don’t pass muster. Nadia: In terms of what I’ve seen on the website, those qualifications are not registered on the NQF. V/O: But Immanuel's website falsely claims that they are. Claire: When you've got a program that is offered and at the bottom it said NQF4 what are you explaining? What are you saying to those people who are trying to apply to a program? VdB: NQF4. So those are those 120 credits. Claire: But those are not recognized by SAQA, are they? Vd Berg: No, they get endorsed by them. Claire: They endorsed by SAQA? VdB: Yeah. They're SAQA moderators, assessors, and some of them become pastors with us. So these guys are SAQA, they got stamps. So our programs are stamped. V/O: Who knows what stamps they’re collecting, but they’re not SAQA’s. Nadia: I don't know the people that he refers to, but anyone working outside of the system, it would seem to me wouldn't have the mandates to make certain decisions. So for those people that have gone through a process that is not really legitimate, their qualifications wouldn’t be recognised. Link: So what do you do when the South African qualifications authority doesn’t register the qualifications you’re dishing out? Well, if you’re a self-appointed Professor like Eddie van den Berg you don’t let that ruin your business plan. You simply create your own Qualifications authority: the CTQA. V/O: Christian Theology Quality Assurance was registered by van den Berg in 2018 at this address in Boksburg. It’s also houses a sex shop, a gambling lounge and a bottle store – en route to the land of milk and honey liqueur. Claire: So what’s the CTQA’s job? VdB: They look after the accreditation of the programs and then when people do RPL, they look if they’ve got it. Claire: So you create the program and they you also make sure that your own program is verified and accredited? VdB: No, that is our teachings. The CTQA is to look at the Christian theology. Claire: But the Christian theology they they’re looking at, it’s yours. It’s the programs that you’ve written? VdB: The programs I wrote. Claire: So the organization that you’ve created is the organization that then verifies the programs that you wrote. VdB: That was the initial thing is that we need accreditation. Because I was asked what are you going to do with SAQA? V/O: We showed the CEO one of the qualification forms issued by CTQA. Nadia: Essentially what he’s done is taken the structure and even some of the wording of our qualifications from our national qualifications register and essentially appropriated it for content that is not quality assured. And in fact even the preamble and some of the sections are in fact very much a copy and paste of our structure. Shaheeda: This is the evidence that he has usurped the functions of SAQA, which is a statutory regulatory body, established in terms of the NQF Act. It wouldn’t be fair for me to say someone is mentally unstable or not okay up there. But this is fraud. V/O: Yet “Prof" Edward refuses to acknowledge that Immanuel’s Diplomas and Degrees are not worth the paper they’re copied and pasted on. Claire: That is not a registered or a recognized qualification that you are handing out. VdB: No, I’m not saying so. Claire: You don’t agree with that? Eddie: No. V/O: Talk about turning a blind eye to a burning bush. Link: It’s like me starting the Derek Watts Dance Academy, or the Carte Blanche University of Sweetness and Light. Sign up now and I’ll get you a Doctorate by Easter. VO: And once you’re a doctor, you can become a Bishop. Claire: So how many Bishops have you ordained? Eddie: I’ve done 12 bishops, of which say, six is Arches and six others. I was ordained or consecrated as a Bishop. That’s under the South African Bishops Council. Pentecostal Bishops Council. I was the visionary of that. Claire: Are you registered with the SA Council of Churches? Eddie: No. Claire: Why? Eddie: Because they’re Trinitarians. V/O: Instead he created the South African Christian Religious Council. Claire: So the SA Religious Council of Churches is also your organization? Eddie: That’s my NPO. Claire: That’s your NPO? Eddie: To make sure that we can ordain and appoint the pastors. Claire: Is that NPO registered in South Africa? Is it recognised? Eddie: Yeah. V/O: But the NPO Certificate he supplied is fake. We checked with the Department of Social Development and this NPO number actually belongs to Sitofini Pre-School in the Eastern Cape. It seems this Archbishop may be an arch fraudster.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Doctor, Professor, Chancellor, Archbishop Edward van der Berg is a self-proclaimed General of God, but the long arm of the law has caught up with him for running a bogus university
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Prophets for profit. Edward van den Berg is a self-appointed Visionary who received a “commission from God" to establish the Immanuel Theology Institute International, formerly known as the Immanuel University of Theology International. That was until 2018 when the Department of Higher Education and Training demanded that van den Berg cease to call it a “university”, as all South African universities are organs of state. Nevertheless there are now 50 (FIFTY) Immanuel campuses across South Africa - from the Immanuel University of Orange Farm to the Immanuel University of Pongola – and another 26 campuses spread across Africa, from Madagascar to Nigeria, not to mention India and Russia. But what do they mean by “campus”? And who runs them? Professor Chancellor Archbishop van den Berg offers Certificates, Diplomas and Degrees, from Bachelors to Masters to Doctorates. And former alumni like Bishop Doctor Bernard Coopasamy of KZN (pictured with President Cyril Ramaphosa at the Law and Religious Communities in Africa conference in 2020)) who go on to open satellite campuses that offer the same courses. But who recognises them? Immanuel Theology Institute is NOT accredited with SAQA. Why not? This is van den Berg’s reason: i. The Christian Theology programs available at SAQA accredited training venues are all of the Trinity Based faith based doctrine of the Roman Catholic Church. ii. We are a unique training Entity for Pentecostal, Charismatic and Free Churches that does not form part of the so called main stream churches that supported the Apartheid System or being part of the Roman Catholic Trinity (Three God Doctrine) doctrine of the Roman Cleric.
metadata.Summary: Ironically, all the self-ordained Bishops and Archbishops are not averse to wearing the liturgical vestments and other paraphernalia that originated in the Roman Catholic church. So where does the Immanuel University/Institute buy their chasubles and mitres? The same place they buy their academic gowns and caps – Distinguished Cuts Mantles in downtown Joburg, who proudly list Archbishop Edward van den Berg as a client. Immanuel University is not registered on the SAQA database and is not accredited to offer NQF-registered qualifications. Not to be discouraged van den Berg simply created his own organisation: CTQA (Christian Theology Quality Assurance Association (Pty) Ltd, This entity was allegedly registered with CIPRO by Chancellor Professor Archbishop van den Berg in 2018. Bishop Coopasamy is the Vice-President. Immanuel’s website gives a long list of other accrediting institutions, but a cursory check proves these claims to be false: Theology Accreditation International does not exist, and Theological Accreditation International has never heard of them. COMENSA has never heard of them. American Accrediting Association of Theological Institutions (A.A.A.T.I.) does not credit any institution outside the USA Ballsbridge University is is listed as a bogus university by the DHET. metadata.Further information: The NQF Amendment Act of 2019: (4) Any person, education institution, skills development provider, foreign institution is guilty of an offence if it falsely claims to be registered and accredited as an education institution, skills development provider or foreign institution in terms of the laws of the Republic or foreign law. If found guilty van der Berg and his co-accused could be fined and face up to 5 years in prison. However, the Immanuel website is still up and running and offering courses at it's various campuses.
